pr_title: Don't do fatal on error writing the health api management key.
pr_body:
##### Summary
<!--
Describe the change in summary section, including rationale and design decisions.
Include "Fixes #nnn" if you are fixing an existing issue.
-->
Fixes #12568 

If for any reason there is trouble committing the Health API management key to disk, don't exit, but instead inform the user to fix the problem and provide the produced api key in the log file. This can be used to access the management API, but only during this session of Netdata.

##### Test Plan

<!--
Provide enough detail so that your reviewer can understand which test cases you
have covered, and recreate them if necessary. If our CI covers sufficient tests, then state which tests cover the change.
-->

Specify a readonly path to save the key (e.g. `/root/something` if running as a normal user) in field `netdata management api key file` under `registry` in `netdata.conf`. Using this PR the agent will keep running, and the printed key can be used to access the API.

issue_context.title: [Bug]: Failure to create a management API key file should not shutdown the agent
issue_context.body:
### Bug description

When the agent fails to create a `management API key file` it will shutdown with a fatal error. It should log an error instead and continue operation. This api key is used in the health management API

### Expected behavior

The agent should start up normally

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure agent so that the `netdata.api.key` resides in a location that cannot be written by the agent on startup by
setting the `"netdata management api key file` location in the `[registry]` section
2. Try to start the agent and notice that it fails

comments:
How would we like to continue when this happens?

1) Disable the api.
2) Create a key in memory, print it in error.log, and allow to work with it while the agent is up. On restart user would need to use a new one again or fix the path.
3) Store this key in sqlite instead of a file, but provide a way for the user to see it:
3a) Migrate the key to sqlite all together
3b) Use both (the file and sqlite, but that would add complexity).
4) Use instead `netdata_configured_varlib_dir` if `netdata management api key file` is not writable ? (But I don't like overriding user config).

review_comments: Just a comment: not sure we need "please" here.
